title: Can the browser filter this list?
description: The browser cached the ten suggestions returned for new. The user adds a space and y. A teammate proposes filtering those ten locally and skipping the new request. The earlier response was truncated to ten out of many matches. What is the correctness risk?

options.text: Filtering is safe because every completion for a longer prefix must be in the shorter prefix's top ten.
options.explanation: The longer-prefix set is a subset of all shorter-prefix matches, not necessarily of its returned top ten.

options.text: Only ranking freshness matters; the earlier top ten still contains every possible new y match.
options.explanation: Truncation removes candidates even if scores never change. Missing longer-prefix candidates are the issue here.

options.text: The browser should filter the earlier list and pad it with personal history to preserve global ranking.
options.explanation: Personal history is a different source and cannot recover the missing popular candidates or prove their rank.

options.text: Fetch the longer prefix's results; local filtering is safe only when the earlier response contained the complete match set.
options.explanation: A candidate below tenth place for new may rank first for new y. A complete shorter-prefix set can be filtered; a truncated one cannot establish the longer prefix's top ten.
